text:
**Verdict**

Score: **5/10**. The project has a coherent structure and some good unit-test intent, but I would not approve it as-is. The main problem is reproducibility: the checked-in repo cannot run the advertised tiny/demo pipeline because `data/stories` is empty, while stale generated outputs are present. There are also several brittle edge cases in extraction/math and some operational issues around HTTP generation and packaging.

I could not run the test suite because this environment has none of the declared dependencies installed (`numpy`, `torch`, `transformers`, `PyYAML`, etc.). Syntax compilation passed when bytecode was redirected to `/tmp`.

**Concrete Issues**

- [config.yaml](/work/config.yaml:11): High - Pipeline points at `data/stories`, but the directory is empty, so `emovec all --tiny` cannot reproduce checked-in outputs.
- [emovec/cli.py](/work/emovec/cli.py:54): High - `generate-stories` tries to read `data/stories/manifest.json` before generation, making story generation impossible from a fresh checkout.
- [emovec/stories.py](/work/emovec/stories.py:71): High - Story loading assumes every configured file exists and has valid content; missing/empty files crash late or poison activations.
- [emovec/model.py](/work/emovec/model.py:123): Medium - One-token or empty-token inputs can make `L - s == 0`, causing division-by-zero in activation averaging.
- [emovec/vectors.py](/work/emovec/vectors.py:66): Medium - PCA has no zero-variance guard; constant/degenerate neutral activations produce NaN ratios/components.
- [emovec/elo.py](/work/emovec/elo.py:44): Medium - Bradley-Terry fitting uses unstable sigmoid/log math without clipping `p_hat`, so large updates can overflow or produce NaN loss.
- [emovec/stories.py](/work/emovec/stories.py:136): Medium - External story-generation HTTP calls have no timeout, so the CLI can hang indefinitely.
- [emovec/stories.py](/work/emovec/stories.py:144): Medium - Generated story files are overwritten directly with no temp-file/atomic write or resume/skip behavior, risking partial corrupted datasets.
- [.gitignore](/work/.gitignore:2): Medium - `*.egg-info/` and `outputs/` are ignored but present in the repo, indicating generated/stale artifacts are being mixed with source.
- [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:12): Medium - Heavy ML dependencies are only lower-bound pinned, so model/runtime behavior is not reproducible across future installs.
- [requirements.txt](/work/requirements.txt:6): Low - `pytest` is included in runtime requirements instead of only dev/test dependencies.
- [tests/test_datasets.py](/work/tests/test_datasets.py:44): Low - Story-loader coverage is skipped when the dataset is absent, exactly the state this checkout is in.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **260 lines**.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Configured story dataset path is empty, so the advertised tiny/demo pipeline is not reproducible from checkout.
generate-stories requires an existing manifest before it can generate the missing story dataset.
Story loading assumes all files exist and contain usable text, causing crashes or bad activations for missing/empty files.
Activation averaging can divide by zero for one-token or empty effective inputs.
PCA does not handle zero-variance activation matrices and can emit NaN components.
Bradley-Terry optimization uses numerically unstable sigmoid/log calculations without clipping predicted probabilities.
Story-generation HTTP requests have no timeout and can hang the CLI indefinitely.
Generated story files are overwritten directly without atomic writes or resume-safe behavior.
Ignored generated artifacts are present in the repo, creating stale output and packaging hygiene risk.
Core ML dependencies use only lower-bound pins, making future installs and model behavior non-reproducible.
Runtime requirements mix application dependencies with pytest instead of keeping test tooling in dev extras.
Dataset validation is skipped when the story dataset is absent, so CI would miss the fresh-checkout failure.
